record.context_brief: Parabolic inverse problem with final data.
record.original_question: Consider the parabolic problem u_t - div(a grad u) = 0 in Omega x (0, T), with boundary condition u = g(x, t) on ∂Omega x (0, T) and initial condition u = h(x) on Omega x {0}, where g and h are to be chosen appropriately and the coefficient a is known on ∂Omega. Does knowledge of the final-time state u(·, T) uniquely determine the coefficient a?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ be a bounded domain with smooth boundary $\partial\Omega$, and let $T > 0$. Consider the parabolic initial-boundary value problem
$$u_t - \operatorname{div}(a(x)\,\nabla u) = 0 \quad \text{in } \Omega \times (0, T),$$
$$u(x,t) = g(x,t) \quad \text{on } \partial\Omega \times (0, T),$$
$$u(x,0) = h(x) \quad \text{in } \Omega,$$
where the scalar coefficient $a : \overline{\Omega} \to (0,\infty)$ is bounded and uniformly positive, and is assumed known on $\partial\Omega$. Determine whether one can choose boundary data $g$ and initial data $h$ (within an appropriate admissible class) so that the single final-time measurement $u(\cdot, T)$ in $\Omega$ uniquely determines the coefficient $a$ throughout $\Omega$.
artifact.status_search_result: The general uniqueness question of recovering the diffusion coefficient $a$ in a parabolic equation from a single final-time observation $u(\cdot,T)$ has been studied with partial results. Under additional spectral concentration assumptions on the elliptic operator and on the initial state, uniqueness and Lipschitz stability (with constants growing exponentially in $T$) have been established. Other works treat related identification problems (e.g., for first-order coefficients or under monotonicity assumptions on $h$). A fully general uniqueness result for arbitrary admissible $(g,h)$ does not appear to be available, and the problem is regarded as significantly ill-posed.

status_evidence.title: Coefficient identification in parabolic equations with final data
status_evidence.snippet: Under assumptions on the concentration of eigenvalues of the elliptic operator and on the initial state, we prove uniqueness... and a Lipschitz stability estimate for the inversion provided that the final time is sufficiently large.
status_evidence.claim: Uniqueness and Lipschitz stability are known under spectral concentration assumptions, indicating partial progress.

status_evidence.title: Identifying the coefficient of first-order in parabolic equation from final measurement data
status_evidence.snippet: An inverse problem of identifying a coefficient in a parabolic equation from final measurement data.
status_evidence.claim: Related identification problems with final data have been studied, with conditional uniqueness results.

status_evidence.title: Inverse parabolic problems by Carleman estimates with data taken at initial or final time moment
status_evidence.snippet: Carleman-estimate-based approach to inverse parabolic problems with final-time data.
status_evidence.claim: Carleman techniques yield conditional stability/uniqueness for various final-data inverse parabolic problems.
